records.title: 10-Q
records.text: The increase in revenues was driven by oil and gas drilling activity levels that improved in every major region of the world, market share gains in certain markets, and higher prices.

records.title: 10-Q
records.text: COVID-19 operational disruptions and supply chain issues negatively impacted the conversion of revenue from backlog during the quarter.

records.title: 10-Q
records.text: New orders booked during the quarter totaled $384 million, representing a book-to-bill of 144 percent when compared to the $266 million of orders shipped from backlog.

records.title: 10-Q
records.text: The average per barrel price of West Texas Intermediate Crude Oil increased seven percent (from $66.09 per barrel to $70.62 per barrel) and natural gas prices increased 48 percent (from $2.91 per mmbtu to $4.32 per mmbtu) in the third quarter of 2021 compared to the second quarter of 2021.

records.title: 10-Q
records.text: Adjusted EBITDA (operating profit excluding depreciation, amortization, and Other Items) decreased sequentially to $56 million, or 4.2 percent of sales.
